![What's new in Hamstr 0.7.4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mailo037/Hamstr/v0.7.4/docs/images/releases/v0.7.4.png)

Hamstr 0.7.4 keeps albums together, gives playlists quick actions and makes the desktop app feel like one.

- **Albums stay albums.** What you stash as an album or playlist is one row under *Stashed*, just as it was one header while downloading: its cover, how many songs, the artist and the size. Tap it to show the songs; a song from it plays on through the album. Swipe the row right to play the album, left to hide it.
- **Hold a playlist** in the library for quick actions: play, shuffle, share its files, play next or add to the queue, rename, delete the playlist (its files stay) or, for a downloaded album, delete its files too.
- **Right-click on the desktop** does what a long press does on the phone, for example the menu of a stashed file. Where the phone swipes, the desktop shows the actions as icons at the end of the row.
- **Swipe in more places.** Swipe a device away in *Devices* to forget it; swipe a hidden file right to show it again or left to delete it.
- **Songs look like songs.** Picking from a playlist with *Audio* chosen, the covers are square.
- **Locked songs, the right ones.** For a Spotify link Hamstr now reads the song's name, artist and length reliably (also from Spotify's player page when the shared link redirects a lot), and without them it asks again instead of guessing from the link. Tags like *#JerseyClub* stay out of the search.

Signed APKs are available for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64 and all ABIs together. The desktop installers aren't signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen and macOS Gatekeeper ask before the first start. Verify every file against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
